_about: Monta T-bar (surface lift, modern), rebuilt to the owner's reference installation: the drive at the bottom (D1) and the return at the top, a tower kit (heads, 1 m mast sections, base; every mast leaning across the line, D11), the carriers (recoil box on its grip, T bar and J bar) and the operator hut. Millimetres in the lift frame: origin on the bullwheel's axle (a terminal) or the mast top (a head) or at grade (a base, mast section, hut), u toward the line (uphill on a tower), v right, w up. The loaded (uphill) rope is on the right going up: v+ at the bottom terminal, v- at the top one.

common._sheave: v3 (R1, R2): 350 dished discs with a thin liner band (rim to dia, ~15 % of the radius)

train._about: A sheave train on one rope: sheaves in pairs on rockers (a cast web inboard, rockerThick, a thin cheek plate outboard, cheekThick), the rockers' pins on a pentagonal equaliser inboard of them, the equaliser on the end pin through the crossarm's end plate. Support trains stand on the pin with the rope on top; hold-down trains hang inverted from the same pin. The axles sit on an arc of radius arcR about the rope's bend. Offsets in v run inboard from the sheave's hub: cheek gap, web, equaliser gap, equaliser, end gap, end plate.

tower._lean: D11/Q1: every mast leans this many degrees across the line toward the loaded track; ropes level, the foundation off to the return side

base._stub: the mast's first stretch is part of the base, wrapped in the red tower pad (D5, plain with a light cap ring at its top, R6); mast_foot at its top along the leaned axis

head._v3: R3 one tall cone from the sleeve to the flange; R4/R26 a square platform ring 1.15 m down the mast with braces to the arm ends; R7 triangular gussets; R27 a diagonal strut to the top bar and curled hook brackets; R29 smooth catchers, longer on the drag (+v) side; R32 octagonal pin covers the arm's depth
head._catcher: black tube out from each end of each train, inside the carrier hanger's D (out of v, below the rope), so a swinging hanger can't reach the sheaves: a smooth sweep outboard and down; lengthDrag on the loaded (+v) side

drive._about: The bottom station (D1): one box column on a concrete block, its lower part the cabinet, a slim side cabinet and gussets at its foot; a head frame of two girders along the line; the bullwheel hung under a hoop-railed grating deck behind the column (the deck ends over the wheel's centre, its back half in the open, R8) with the machinery house on it (louvres on its back end, windows on its -v side); toward the line a separate narrower platform a step down (trainDeck.drop) over two hold-down trains (8 sheaves on the leaving loaded rope, v+, 4 on the arriving one); the loading hoop just under the leaving train on a short rod from a bracket off its girder, outboard of the bars (R12). No braces, no ladder (R10, R11). Rope at 3.4 m (D8).
drive._hoop: the loading hoop (R12): a black ring in the u-w plane hanging just under the loaded train on a short rod from a bracket off its girder, outboard of the bars' path where the operator steadies them

return._about: The top station: one tapered box column leaning back toward the wheel, hinged at its foot, and a plumb box strut on a flat pad, carrying the girders bare (R16): a hoop-railed grating platform over the trains and another round the bearing beside the wheel, the box-section gallows for the wire between them (R17); the bullwheel cantilevered behind on its shaft from a bearing housing (the tensioning hidden inside, D2); 8-sheave hold-down trains on both ropes toward the line; a thin guard rail round the wheel and along the trains (R18); a galvanised ladder up the column's line face to the trains' platform, whose railing opens at its head. Rope at 4.5 m (Q4).

hut._about: The operator hut (D9, Q3): red walls on skids, a mono-pitch white roof falling toward +u, the door and a window on the -u face, a window each side.

carrier._about: Carriers: a small dark clamp grip on the rope's outboard side; from it one hanger tube sweeps outboard and down in a half ellipse (the rope its straight side, a D) and comes back in to the recoil box, a pale rounded housing that hangs on a pin through its upper part, swinging fore and aft, nearly back under the rope; the cord leaves a collar at its bottom. The bar: a yellow stem with a plain socket at its top where the cord ends, and one continuous black padded crossbar (T) or a yellow J curve. Grip origin on the rope; u the way the carrier travels, +v outboard, w up. The bars' origin at their eye (the socket's top).

grip._grip: the clamp outboard of the sheaves' faces (vIn past the sheave's half width), its thin jaw reaching in to the rope inside the liners' clearance, so it passes support and hold-down sheaves and the bullwheel's groove (C12)
